items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So, he talked to Earl Hood and Earl Hood gave me a chance to play in his band. So I went to rehearse and he liked me and I joined his band.

ctx.x: Did your mother live in Columbus her whole life?

Oh yeah, when she left Kentucky, she left for good. She left there when I was six months old and she stayed. She did come back to see me just about every year but one time she was called, I was very sick. I had typhoid, and at that time there was no antidote for typhoid fever. I don’t know how I attracted it, I was about eight years old or nine years old, but the fever was just doing me in and the doctor had given me up. He said I’ve tried everything as a country doctor that he knew. So my grandmother, the one…

tuxedo. So my mother bought me a tuxedo. And on weekends we’d go to all the little places around, I used to play a lot where the Mills Brothers were born in Pickaway, OH. We’d go to all the little neighboring places around Ohio and I never got paid. Most of them were getting 35 cents for the night and he’d pass over me, so when I’d get to my mother, she’d say to me, “Where’s the money?”. items.q: I'll tell you who was playing with the band, a guy named Paul Tyler, who was a great saxophone player with Captain Wormack's band

ctx.x: Well, then your mother did take you back to Columbus?

Oh, yes, when I got 12 years old she came and took me back to Columbus, Ohio. And there was a fantastic trumpet player at the time, a great friend of Sy Oliver's. He had a band around there named Pete France. Pete France, yes. Great man. He had a band around Columbus, Ohio. I'll tell you who was playing with the band, a guy named Paul Tyler, who was a
great saxophone player with Captain Wormack's band, you remember ever seeing pictures of a band, Captain Wormack?
